steps.text: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in garlic; cook until fragrant, 1 to 3 minutes. Stir in dried basil; cook a few seconds more.
Add tomatoes, sugar, onion powder, garlic powder, red pepper flakes, black pepper, and salt. Bring to a simmer; stir in cucumber and bell pepper.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, until mixture reduces and thickens, 10 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cucumber-Tomato Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Try this cucumber-tomato sauce recipe in place of traditional pasta sauce for an alternative take on a vegetable sauce with big flavor in every bite.
raw_recipe.name: Cucumber-Tomato Sauce

review.reviewBody: Never seen or had a sauce combining cucumber & tomato. In fact, I never had a cooked cucumber ( I think..). But my tiny (not even that) garden produced a few tomatoes & cucumbers and I was at loss what to do with them. so I typed "tomato sauce" and I came up with this one.. I am a beginner, bad one at that. I am far better at booking restaurant reservation than knowing kitchen jargons. ie. I know when I taste good one but I would never be able to cook one. Well, this tastes great when I cooked it.. I am thinking, I can eat this with chips, perhaps french bread, if all fail, I will just eat this sauce as a meal. WONDERFUL!

I was truly surprised how good this was. Had NEVER cooked cucumber in any type of recipe and the only reason I made this was because I needed to use a cucumber and I was tired of eating it raw in salads! I did use chopped sweet onion and I sauteed it with the bell pepper, garlic & basil before adding the rest of the ingredients to simmer. I used a potato masher to make the sauce a slightly smoother consistency and served it mixed with rotini pasta.

I gave the recipe 4 stars only because I added a few things of my own. I used 6 medium tomatoes, to make it more tomatoei, I used a chocolate pepper instead of red, and I added a pobllano pepper. I also cooked it longer. I like letting sauces simmer for a while and digest if you will. I topped it off with a few sprigs of rosemary, and it was amazing! I'll definitly make it again!
Good recipe. I put grilled sausages in it and placed it over spaghetti squash (baked cut size down at 350 degrees with garlic butter) and it was delicious!

Made this one and everyone loved it. Even the veggie-phobes. The cucumbers give it a sweet taste that is unexpected in a sauce. I used a can of fire roasted tomatoes and a little less sugar. Easy-peasy and all gone!

This recipe appealed to me due to the over productive cucumbers in my garden. I used only 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes, and it still had a little too much spice for my children. I also used just 2 tsp sugar on the advice of other reviewers. I'll use 1 1/2 tsp next time. While I won't make this recipe frequently, it's a good way to add some variety with summer garden abundance.

This is a delightful, fresh tasting sauce with a twist. I put it over angel hair pasta. My husband and I enjoyed the flavors. My advice is to taste the sauce after 2 tsp. of sugar are added and decide if you want to add the rest. I stopped at 2 1/2, any more would have been way too much for our taste.

My mother and I loved this; my father pushed it away after a couple of mouthfuls, finding it too sweet. It was very sweet, and I will cut the sugar in half next time, but will definitely make it again; I loved the combination of the veggies.

Really enjoyed this. Like many who hadn't, I braised cucumbers after seeing Julie and Julia and loved them, so cooking cukes didn't worry me as it might have otherwise. Did cut the sugar as suggested, I think the cukes must counteract the acidicity of the tomatoes, so unsure if sugar is even necessary at all. My only complaint is that I shouldn't have made pasta ;) just the sauce and the crusty homemade pain du sel would've been okay by me.

My fiance, who doesn't like cucumber raw, LOVED this recipe. He kept asking what spices were in it. I added less than a tsp of sugar, just enough to take away the bite. I followed the rest of the recipe exactly. Thanks for sharing!!
The cucumber-tomato combination didn't taste well to us. It was very hearty and fun to make, just a little too different and sweet for our taste.

When I found too much cucumber in my refrigerator, and was tired of the same old cucumber recipe, I searched the site and found this recipe. I must admit; I wasn't completely sold when I read it, but I thought I'd give it a try - and I was not let down! I absolutely love this recipe - and my family loved it too! The only thing I really did different was substitute the dried seasonings for a general Italian seasoning mix. Other than cutting the vegetables up into pieces that were slightly too big (I'll go smaller next time), I wouldn't change a thing!
I liked it, used less sugar. I thought it was very spicy, but my husband didn't think it was at all. It was good and something different.
I love this sauce!!! Everyone in my family loves it!!! Just one thing you really don't need as much sugar as it says.

I was expecting an Italian flavored sauce that I'd throw in the freezer. What I got was an amazingly flavored sauce with a Thai flair! Something in it - maybe the cucumber seeds have the consistency of ground nuts. There is a slight heat to it, as well. I envision using it as a marinade, a sauce or a dressing. It's delicious.
This was a great recipe. I really enjoyed it!

gorgeous ! and great for using up the last bits in the fridge ....... i added chopped celery and used onion flakes instead...straight into my recipe box... and if you puree it even the kids wont complain !! thank you
The sauce was very hearty. My husband thought too sweet. I thought the cucumbers (main ingredient) were not good in combination with the other ingredients.
